title: Day 12 · 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel (BBC)
desc: Prof Francis Halzen wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for leading the IceCube observatory at the South Pole, built to detect 'ghost particles' called neutrinos from distant galaxies.

title: Day 11 · Children’s books with Black main characters down 8% in a year, study shows (Guardian)
desc: New research into UK publishing shows children’s books with Black main characters fell by almost 8% last year, while disabled representation in picture books dropped sharply too.

title: Day 10 · Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss, threatening water supplies (BBC)
desc: New data shows Swiss glaciers lost more than 5% of their remaining ice in the past 12 months. Scientists warn the rapid melting could threaten water supplies for farming, hydropower and transport in the decades ahead.

title: Day 9 · ‘Hugely exciting’ finds on tiny Scottish island shed light on spread of Christianity (Guardian)
desc: Community-funded excavations on the Scottish island of Lismore have uncovered a sixth-century monastery with rare traces of gold- and silver-working, rewriting the island’s story.

title: Day 8 · Greek PM urges Burnham to return Elgin Marbles permanently (BBC)
desc: Greek PM Kyriakos Mitsotakis urges Andy Burnham to find the political will to send the Parthenon sculptures back to Greece for good, rejecting the British Museum's suggestion that the Bayeux Tapestry loan offers a template for a deal. (BBC News, 24 September 2026.)

title: Day 7 · Oxford lets OpenAI train its AI models on Bodleian Library (Guardian)
desc: Internal documents show the University of Oxford has let OpenAI train its AI models on historical texts from its Bodleian Library, while staff minutes record concerns over reputational risk. (The Guardian, 26 September 2026.)

title: Day 6 · Library's first edition reveals Austen's early fans (BBC)
desc: A first edition of Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility at Longleat House reveals how her novels were read and collected by the country-house elite during her lifetime.

title: Day 5 · Novelist accused of using AI to write book removed from French prize list (Guardian)
desc: France's most prestigious literary prize withdraws a Canadian-Haitian writer's novel from its longlist after an anonymous X account alleged it was 'almost entirely' written by AI — the author denies the claim and calls it racially motivated. (The Guardian, 25 September 2026.)

title: Day 4 · Autumn by Kate Mosse review – tender reflections on time and place (Guardian)
desc: Ruth Padel reviews Kate Mosse's new book Autumn — a love-song to West Sussex and a meditation on the turning of the seasons. (The Guardian, 22 September 2026.)

title: Day 3 · Bonnie Greer, British-American author and critic, dies aged 77 (BBC)
desc: The pioneering novelist and theatre critic, first black president of the Edinburgh International Festival, has died.

title: Day 2 · Emily Wilson to retranslate the Odyssey from scratch (Guardian)
desc: The Oxford classicist who made Homer plain-English starts again from scratch.

title: Day 1 · Ancient Roman shipwreck discovered off Sicily coast (BBC)
desc: 2000-year-old Roman wreck with amphorae hoard found near Mazara del Vallo.
